terra.problem: The reference to heavy words earlier in Amos is a fact from outside the passage without a supporting reference.
The verse does not say that part of the tent is still standing or that the LORD will build on what remains.
Calling Edom a neighbor adds a geographical fact not established by the passage, without a supporting reference.
Calling Philistia and Moab close neighbors adds a geographical fact from outside the passage without a supporting reference.
Saying the promise does not go to Egypt or Cush goes beyond the text, which does not identify every nation that bears the LORD's name. The final sentence also leaves out those nations.
Calling Edom right next door adds a geographical fact not established by the passage, without a supporting reference.
It presents the size of the harvest as the reason the plowman overtakes the reaper. The verse does not give that reason.
The verse does not say everybody is on time.
The verse does not say the reaper is leaving nothing behind.
The verse says they will rebuild and inhabit the cities; it does not state their intentions about selling property.
Amos 5:11 says they will not drink the wine; it does not say the wine will no longer belong to them.
